name: broken
summary: A check whose query names a table that does not exist.
explanation: It cannot run, so it is reported as an error under its own name. Fix the query.

name: one-record-view-per-aggregate
summary: Each aggregate has exactly one Record view use case.
explanation: S2's house rule: one use case follows the Record view pattern for each aggregate, naming the aggregate in its record setting. Write the missing use case, or merge the extra ones.
query:
WITH views AS (
  SELECT v.value AS aggregate, v.follower_id AS use_case
  FROM setting_value v
  JOIN pattern p ON p.id = v.pattern_id AND p.title = 'Record view'
  JOIN use_case u ON u.id = v.follower_id
  WHERE v.setting = 'record'
)
-- The query's own check column is ignored: the row's name is the check's name.
SELECT 'house-rule' AS "check", a.id AS record,
       'Aggregate ' || a.id || ' has ' || count(v.use_case) || ' Record view use cases'
       || CASE WHEN count(v.use_case) > 0 THEN ' (' || string_agg(v.use_case, ', ' ORDER BY v.use_case) || ')' ELSE '' END
       || '; it needs exactly one.' AS message
FROM aggregate a
LEFT JOIN views v ON v.aggregate = a.id
GROUP BY a.id
HAVING count(v.use_case) <> 1
ORDER BY a.id
